questions.prompt: What is the idiomatic multiple-return signature for a function that can fail?
questions.explanation: Go functions return the useful value plus an `error` last; the caller checks `if err != nil`. Go has no exceptions.

questions.prompt: When are the arguments to a deferred call evaluated?

options.text: When the deferred call actually executes at return
Never — deferred calls take no arguments

questions.explanation: Deferred arguments are captured when `defer` executes, even though the call itself runs when the surrounding function returns.

questions.prompt: Multiple `defer` statements run in ____ order (three-letter abbreviation) when the function returns.
questions.explanation: Deferred calls run last-in, first-out: the most recently deferred call runs first.

questions.prompt: Which statements about functions in Go are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Functions are first-class values (can be stored and passed)
A closure captures variables from its surrounding scope
A trailing `...T` parameter accepts any number of arguments
`defer` runs at the end of each loop iteration

questions.explanation: Functions are first-class, closures capture scope, and variadic `...T` collects arguments into a slice. `defer` runs at function return, not per loop iteration.

questions.prompt: In `_, err := f()`, what does the blank identifier `_` do?

options.text: Discards the first returned value, keeping only err

questions.explanation: The blank identifier discards the value in that position, so you keep only the ones you care about.

questions.prompt: Match each function feature to its purpose.

pairs.right: Guarantee cleanup on every exit path
Return values that a bare return sends back
Bundle behavior with private captured state

questions.explanation: Each feature serves a distinct role; defer is especially valuable because it runs even when the function panics.
